faq.question: How much does craft beer cost in Singapore?
faq.answer: Craft beer typically costs S$10–$22 per pint. Hawker center spots like Smith Street Taps are S$10–$16, while LeVeL33 charges S$14–$22. Happy hours bring prices to S$10–$12. Modestly priced vs London/NYC, pricier than Bangkok.

faq.question: What local Singapore craft breweries should I try?
faq.answer: Key local breweries: Lion Brewery Co (Straits Pale Ale), Brewerkz (since 1997), Little Island Brewing Co, RedDot Brewhouse, Pink Blossoms Brewing, and 1965 Craft Beer. SG Taps on Duxton Hill pledges half their 20 taps to local brewers.

faq.question: What's the best neighborhood for craft beer?
faq.answer: No single district — bars are scattered. Duxton Hill has SG Taps near Lion Brewery Co. Jalan Besar has Druggists. Robertson Quay has Gulp near Brewerkz. Tiong Bahru has Canjob. Bar crawl: SG Taps → Lion Brewery → Druggists.

faq.question: Is Singapore's craft beer scene worth exploring as a tourist?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Singapore punches above its weight with bars rivaling Tokyo, Portland, or Copenhagen. Unique elements: Asian-fusion flavors (yuzu lagers, tropical IPAs), hawker center pairing culture, and world-class venues like LeVeL33.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit?
faq.answer: Most bars open afternoons (2–5pm) until 11pm–1am. Weekday happy hours (3–7pm) offer best value. Thu–Sat are peak nights. Smith Street Taps only opens Thu–Sun. Singapore's tropical climate means cold craft beer is welcome year-round.

faq.question: Can I do a craft beer bar crawl?
faq.answer: Yes! Route: Smith Street Taps (Chinatown) → SG Taps (Duxton Hill, 10 min walk) → Lion Brewery Co (Club St, 5 min) → Druggists (Jalan Besar, taxi) → Ziggy Zaggy (Kampong Bugis, 5 min). 5 bars, ~4 hours, S$60–$100.
